articles.title: How Do You Know That You Love Somebody? Philosopher Martha Nussbaum’s Incompleteness Theorem of the Heart’s Truth, from Plato to Proust
articles.highlight: 爱与否认爱、受苦与否认受苦之间的交替，构成了人心最本质、最普遍的结构特征。
articles.summary: 文章借哲学家玛莎·努斯鲍姆之口，从柏拉图到普鲁斯特，探讨爱与认识之间的关系。核心观点是：我们无法像证明数学定理一样一劳永逸地确认“我爱某人”，因为爱的真相本就呈现为爱与否认、痛苦与否认痛苦之间的反复交替。理解这一内在波动，比追求一种确定的情感答案更贴近人心真相。
articles.failureAnalysis: 核心启示：要承认爱的本质包含怀疑和动摇，不必追求永恒不变的确定性。认识人心，应接受其反复与矛盾，而非试图找到单一答案。
articles.sourceExcerpt: "The alternations between love and its denial, suffering and denial of suffering … constitute the most essential and ubiquitous structural feature of the human heart."

articles.title: Quoting Linus Torvalds
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: No clear evidence
articles.summary: 本文引用林纳斯·托瓦兹的评论，描述一次艰难的内核调试过程。AI 多次想放弃，但在持续推进下仍完成了大量调试工作，因此托瓦兹让 AI 撰写提交信息。这展示了生成式 AI 在真实编程中的价值与局限。

articles.sourceExcerpt: And this was a debug session from hell, enormously helped by an AI doing much of the grunt-work. I'd like to call it my tireless helper, but the AI several times stated flat out that this was impossible and unsolvable and that we should just write a report about it. I suspect those things have been trained by people who may not be quite as stubborn as I am.

en.highlight: But while the AI was ready to give up several times, it did keep adding debug code and analyzing it faithfully when I pushed.
en.summary: This article quotes Linus Torvalds describing a hellish kernel debug session greatly helped by an AI. The AI repeatedly said the problem was unsolvable, yet kept adding debug code and analyzing it faithfully when pushed, so Torvalds let it write the commit message. It shows both the value and limits of generative AI in real-world programming.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway is that AI's tendency to give up may reflect human habits in training data, and human persistence is needed to leverage its assistance. This is not a failure but a hallmark of human-AI collaboration.

en.summary: This article, titled 'MCP is dead?', questions the value and sustainability of the Model Context Protocol in real AI applications. The high engagement on Hacker News—400 points and 410 comments—shows strong developer disagreement and makes the engineering and ecosystem reality worth examining.
en.failureAnalysis: Protocols like MCP depend on ecosystem and network effects; if integration costs outweigh benefits, developers won't adopt the standard. Facing competition from proprietary APIs and alternative standards, MCP risks fragmentation and marginalization once initial enthusiasm fades.
en.title: Is MCP Dead? A Look at the Model Context Protocol's Status
